# O R D I N A L L. Chap. 5.

Your liquids are ordained to add and subtract,
To create balance <note>original: "equalitie"</note> through the wisdom of testing <term>assay: the testing of a substance to determine its ingredients and quality</term>;
But do not believe that anything can be
Both hot and moist in the same degree:
For all who believe two qualities can coexist this way
Shall be deceived wherever they go.
Common schools (which teach this) are not correct;
Leave that opinion, and learn this instead:
All the ancients <note>original: "Old men"</note> were mistaken <note>original: "overseene"</note> in this,
To place any two qualities in the same degree;
Otherwise, they said so only so that scholars would not find
The secret mixtures of the elemental kinds.
Therefore, he who does not know his graduations <note>The specific levels or intensities of elemental qualities like heat and moisture</note>
Cannot be perfect in our operations:
For *God* made everything in true number;
Without true number, no man can truly sing;
He who fails in his numbering fails in his song;
He who fails with us must do wrong to nature.

Consider also the nature of the medium <note>original: "meane"</note>,
When it is purified <note>original: "made cleane"</note> to the third degree;
The purer your mediums are,
The more perfection you shall see in them.
These mediums retain a great part
Of the virtues of this *Art* <note>The "Art" of Alchemy</note>:
For the Starting Principle <note>The initial substance or cause</note> cannot exert influence
Upon the final end—nor can there be a flowing back <note>original: "refluence"</note>
To its principle—without the help and aid
Of mediums that contain the extremes mentioned before.
For just as by means of a triple spirit,
The soul of man is joined <note>original: "knit"</note> to his body,
Of which three spirits, one is called *Vital*,
The second is called the *Natural* spirit,
The third spirit is the *Animal* spirit,

--- Page 104 ---
<meta>This page continues Thomas Norton's explanation of the "mediums" or intermediaries necessary in alchemy. He uses the human body—specifically the relationship between the physical body, the immortal soul, and the tripartite "spirits"—as a microcosm for how alchemical substances must be joined using a middle substance.</meta>

<margin>Chapter 5</margin>

And where they dwell, you shall now learn:
The Vital Spirit dwells in the heart,
The Natural Spirit, as the ancient authors tell us,
Is said to dwell in the liver;
But the Animal Spirit <note>Derived from the Latin *anima* (soul); in medieval physiology, this spirit was believed to govern sensation and movement</note> dwells in the brain.
And as long as these three spirits
Continue in a man in their prosperity <note>health or vigorous state</note>,
So long the soul, without any strife,
Will dwell with the body in a prosperous life.
But when these spirits can no longer remain in a man,
The soul immediately departs at that time.
For the subtle soul, pure and immortal,
Can never dwell together with the gross <note>dense or material</note> body—
He is so heavy, and she so light and clean—
If it were not for the subtlety of this spirit acting as a medium <note>original: "meane"</note>.
Therefore, in our work, as the authors teach us,
There must be *Body, Soul, and Spirit* <note>original: "Corpus Anima & Spiritus"</note>.
Also, in our work, you shall find
That our mediums <note>original: "meanes"</note> must accord in every kind
With both extremes, sought out with wisdom;
Otherwise, all our work shall turn clearly to nothing.
For prudent Nature may not, by its working,
Complete the desire <note>original: "Complement of appetite"</note> of a thing,
And so pass between extremes,
Unless she first passes through all the degrees
Of every medium <note>original: "meane"</note>; this is the unfeigned truth.
For this reason, Nature ordained many mediums.

Now, after all this, you need to learn
About the seven circulations of the elements for your success <note>original: "speede"</note>,
According to the number of the seven planets—
Which no man knows unless he has grace from heaven.

But our circulation is from Fire on high,

Towards the matters of harmony <note>original: "concordance"</note>,

Both in substance <note>original: "Matter"</note> and also in shape,

Other vessels are made of stone,

Among workmen, none have yet been found

And yet endure dry fire as well;
Such large stones for our purposes
Would be a precious instrument.
All other vessels are made of glass,
So that the spiritual substances <note>the volatile vapors or "spirits" produced during heating</note> should not escape;
In this land <note>England</note>, every single one is made

Of our glasses, you shall find
That the better kind is the "morning batch" <note>original: "morning stuffe"</note>,
Which was merely ashes the night before,
Having stood in the heat all night and more.

# The Breviary

"What answer will you give me? Let me hear."
"Master," said I, "I grant your desire."

"Then, Son," said he, "keep this oath; I charge you well,
As you think to be saved from the pit of Hell."
The next day we went to church, and after our devotion,
A priest, in his kindness, heard both our confessions;
Which being done, straight to Mass we went,
And he administered the holy Sacrament to us;
But he never knew <note>original: "wist"</note> what we meant by it,
For with a deceptive argument <note>original: "contrary reason"</note> I blinded him.
And so home to dinner we went to our host,
For which entire meal <note>original: "resection"</note> I paid the cost.

When dinner was done, I walked in the field,
Large and open, where people pass by but seldom <note>original: "field," likely a transcription error in the original for "seld," an archaic word for seldom used to maintain the rhyme</note>.
And when we were in the midst, "Boy," said he, "go pick a thistle,
And do not come again until I whistle for you."

"Now, Master," said I, "the coast is clear of listeners."
Then said he, "My son, listen in your ear."
And within three or four words, he revealed to me
The great mystery of the <term>prudence of minerals</term> <note>The wisdom or "prudence" of minerals refers to the hidden properties and governing principles of metallic transformation in alchemy.</note>.

When I heard this, my spirits were ravished with joy;
The Grecians were never gladder for the winning of Troy
Than I was then, remembering my good master even then <note>original: "thoe," an archaic form of "then" used to rhyme with "show"</note>;
For he showed me that very same secret.
Nine days, and no more, I certainly stayed <note>original: "tarried"</note> with him;
But, Lord, in this time, what secrets of nature
He opened to me at various different times,
As I have partly told you in my former rhymes.
The rest is not to be written, on pain of damnation,
Otherwise, I would truly tell of it in this book.
"Now, Father," said I, "I will depart from you,
And I will pray for you wherever I go."
"Son," said he, "God’s blessing go with you and yours,
And if you succeed <note>original: "speed"</note> well, let me hear from you again."

# CHAPTER VII.

A perfect Master you may truly <note>original: "trowe"</note> call him,
Who knows his heats, both high and low.
Nothing may hinder <note>original: "let"</note> your desires more
Than ignorance of the heats of your fires.
In many authors' writings you may see:
"Everything consists in the management of fire" <note>original Latin: *Totum consistit in ignis regimine*</note>;
Therefore, in all chapters you must proceed so
That heat works neither more nor less than is needed;
In this, many of *Geber’s* cooks <note>Geber (Jabir ibn Hayyan) was a legendary 8th-century alchemist. His "cooks" refers to practitioners who followed his chemical recipes literally or clumsily.</note>
Were deceived, though they are wise in books.
The kind of heat with which a pig or goose is scalded,
In this art is called <term>decoction</term> <note>The process of boiling or heating a substance in a liquid to extract its essence.</note>;
For mineral means such heat serves well,
And to make our <term>litharge</term> <note>Litharge is a mineral form of lead oxide, often used in refining metals.</note> "sweat" or release its vapors.
The kind of heat that dries fine linen handkerchiefs
Serves for our "Air" in thirty operations;
But for <term>divisions</term> <note>In alchemy, the separation of a substance into its constituent parts or elements.</note> you must use such heat
As cooks make when they roast thick meat;
The same heat with a circular fire <note>A furnace or fire arranged to provide even, surrounding heat to a vessel.</note>,
We desire for the separation of those parts to be divided;
But for the circulation of elements,
A "glowing fire" <note>original Latin: *Ignis candens*</note> fulfills our intentions;
This fire must always be perfectly equal
At every minute, and yet perpetual;
For it may never diminish nor increase,
And yet the fire may never stop.
Study wisely and look around
To truly <unclear>find out</unclear> such a <unclear>fire</unclear>.
And in that fire, no moisture may be
That the hand may feel or the eye may see.

<margin>Chap. 7.</margin> *Moist fire* <note>original Latin: *Ignis humidus*</note> is another kind of fire also,
And yet it seems like a *contradiction in terms* <note>original Latin: *oppositum in adjecto*</note>:
Such heat separates at certain times
Substances clinging to the sides of the vessels.
This heat can accomplish many more things;
It often makes thick substances thin.
A philosopher spoke unclearly <note>original: "mistely"</note> of this heat,
And said that reaching the highest degree of it
Shall cause and produce such *dryness* <note>original: *Siccitie*</note>
As would be found in the first degree of dry heat.
Another fire is the fire of *drying* <note>original: *Disiccation*</note>,
For substances which are saturated with *moisture* <note>original: *Humectation*</note>.
Another fire is the fire of *preservation* <note>original: *Conservation*</note>,
For all dry things during its operation:
For <term>Magnesia</term> <note>A common but cryptic alchemical term for various mineral ores or the "raw material" of the Stone.</note> is a fire of pouring out <note>original: "effusion"</note>,
Full of perils and full of illusion;
Not only the danger that may ruin the *Work*,
But also that which shall harm the *Master* [alchemist];
Against which, once it is inhaled, there is no remedy <note>original: "boote"</note>;
Therefore, arrange things so you can draw your breath from your feet <note>This is a practical safety warning to avoid inhaling toxic heavy metal fumes by keeping one’s head away from the vessel’s opening.</note>;
Provide protection for your mouth, eyes, ears, and nose,
For it is worse than ten times a *head cold* <note>original: *Pose*</note>.
Men have suffered sore pains because of this,
Because they did not have this warning before.
*Corrosive fire* <note>original Latin: *Ignis corrodens*</note> serves in this *Art*
To wisely separate *closely related elements* <note>original Latin: *Elementa propinqua*</note>.
By one degree of excess, your entire *Work* is ruined <note>original: "shent"</note>,
And one degree too little is insufficient;
Whoever can be sure to find the true degree
Shall be a *great master of fire* <note>original Latin: *Magister magnus in igne*</note>.
It is all the harder to truly know its power
Because there is no way to test it except by our eyesight:
Therefore, all men fail in its presence,
Where heat is learned only at the cost of *experience*.

<header>ORDINARY OF ALCHEMY</header>

<margin>Chapter 7.</margin>
Regarding this heat in particular, *Anaxagoras* said this:
> *No one is found to be discerning at first glance.* <note>original Latin: *Nemo primo fronte reperitur discretus.*</note>

Another is the Heat of mighty Coaction <note>The heat of "coaction" refers to a forced or intense heat used to compel substances to bond or change.</note>,
For minerals that are difficult to liquefy:
This heat cannot be too strong,
No matter how long it is continued.
Another is the Heat of Calcination <note>original: "Calcination" — the process of reducing a substance to powder or ash by heat.</note>
For purifying "foul" metals during their preparation;
This heat must not burn them, nor melt them,
For if it did, they would all soon be ruined <note>original: "spilte"</note>.
The twelfth is the heat used to sublime <note>original: "Sublime" — the process of turning a solid directly into vapor to purify it.</note>
All the "spirits" of the mine <note>Volatile mineral substances like sulfur or mercury.</note>.
The last heat of these serves for all,
When our <term>Stone</term> reaches the stage of Projection <note>The final stage where the "Philosopher's Stone" is cast upon base metal to transmute it into gold.</note>.
Practice makes mastery, there is no more to say,
But he who fails must start again.
Now I have taught you everything by name,
Just as people teach others the way to *Walsingham* <note>A famous site of religious pilgrimage in Norfolk, England; Norton uses it as an analogy for a well-mapped journey.</note>,
Describing every village, water, bridge, and hill,
So that wise men may complete their journey:
So a scholar may find the truth of this science
By this doctrine, if he is clear of mind;
Anyone else may find himself a fool
To meddle with it, if he has little education;
For this is the pinnacle of all worldly knowledge,
Which neither Pope nor King can attain
By their honors, nor by their great councils,
But only by virtue and grace, as authors tell.
This precious <term>Stone</term> will not be found or created
Unless it is sought with true devotion.
The authors named before, along with this book of mine,
Show the entire doctrine of <term>Alchemy</term>,
If you complete all their instructions,
Not according to your own opinion, but following this <term>Ordinall</term> <note>An "ordinal" is a book of rules or directions, specifically for religious services, here used as a title for Norton's definitive guide.</note>;

->Q<-

<page-num>106</page-num>

<header>Norton's</header>

<margin>Chapter 7.</margin> For in this *Ordinal* <note>original: "Ordinall" — a book of rules or directions, specifically Thomas Norton's *Ordinal of Alchemy*.</note> I free you from all doubt:
Nothing is set down incorrectly, nor is one point left out.
There were days when this *Doctrine* and foundation
Would have pleased me more than a thousand pounds;
Three hundred pounds was not what I desired
As much as this *Chapter* on Fire <note>original: "Fier"</note> would have been.
And do not marvel, Lords, nor all you friends,
Why such a noble *Science*, as all men call this *Art*,
Is set out here in *English* that is blunt and plain <note>original: "rude"</note>,
For it is written this way to teach a multitude
Of uneducated <note>original: "rude"</note> people who deal with these works—
Ten thousand *Laymen* <note>people who are not experts or scholars</note> for every ten able *Scholars* <note>original: "Clerks"</note>:
Whereby every year great riches in this *Land*
Are foolishly <note>original: "lewdly"</note> lost, as wise men understand;
And many men of every social rank
Are brought every year to great poverty.
Cease, *Laymen*, cease; do not remain in folly forever;
To leave ignorance <note>original: "lewdness"</note> behind is better late than never.
All those who take pleasure in reading this book,
Pray for my soul, and for all people, both the living <note>original: "Quick"</note> and the dead.
In the year of *Christ*, one thousand four hundred
->and seventy-seven,<-
This work was begun; *Honor be to God in Heaven.*

## Title of the Work <note>original: "Titulus Operis"</note>

Here begins *The Compound of Alchemy*,
Made by a Canon <note>original: "Chanon"; a member of a religious order attached to a cathedral or abbey</note> of *Bridlington*,
Following his learning in *Italy*
At *Exning* <note>original: "Yxning"; a village in Suffolk</note> where he lived <note>original: "wonne"</note> for a time:
In which are openly declared
The secrets of both the *Sun* and *Moon* <note>In alchemy, the Sun and Moon represent Gold and Silver, or the masculine and feminine principles of the Work</note>,
Showing how they must dwell <note>original: "wonne"</note> together in one body
In order to multiply their kind.

This Canon was named <note>original: "hight"</note> Sir *George Ripley*,
Exempt from cloistered <note>original: "Claustrall"</note> observance <note>Relieved from the strict monastic duty of remaining within the cloister walls</note>,
For whom you should pray both day and night,
Since he labored for your advancement.
He turned darkness into light,
Intending to help you toward good fortune <note>original: "happy chaunce"</note>,
Giving counsel that you live rightly,
Doing nothing to displease God.

# GEORGE RIPLEY
## UNTO
### King EDWARD the Fourth.

*O Honorable Lord, and most victorious Knight,*
*With Grace and Fortune abundantly endowed,*
*The safeguard of England, and maintainer of right;*
*That God loves you indeed, He has well shown:*
*Therefore I trust this Land shall be renewed*
*With Joy and Riches, with Charity and Peace,*
*So that old rancors <note>original: "ranckers"; bitter, long-standing resentments or ill will</note> suppressed <note>original: "understrewed"; literally "strewn under," meaning to be trampled down or overcome</note>,*
*Tempestuous troubles and wretchedness shall cease.*

*And now since <note>original: "syth"</note> I see by signs <note>original: "tokens"</note> quite evident,*
*That God guides you, and that you are virtuous,*
*Hating sin, and those who are insolent,*
*And how also Manslaughter is odious to you,*
*And that you are compassionate <note>original: "piteous"; full of pity or mercy</note> toward the indigent,*
*Great pity <note>original: "ruth"</note> it would be if you should not live long:*
*For in your great fortune you are not presumptuous,*
*Nor vengeful of mind to avenge <note>original: "wreke"</note> every wrong.*

*These things considered, along with others, in your most noble Estate,*
*Just as God knows, and people bear witness,*
*It so entirely moves me, that I must certainly <note>original: "algate"; in every way or at all costs</note>*
*Record the same, and therein be no flatterer:*
*And not only that, but also to write here,*
*And to your Highness humbly to present*
*Great Secrets which I learned <note>original: "lere"</note> in far countries,*
*And which by grace are lent to me, though I am most unworthy.*

# The Epistle

I once promised such things to your Lordship,
At the time you commanded me to send them to you;
And since then, I wrote in a very secret manner
To your Grace from the University
Of Louvain <note>original: "Lovayne"; a city in modern-day Belgium, home to a major university where Ripley studied</note>, when God granted me the fortune by Grace to see
Greater secrets and much more profit,
Which I will only disclose to you:
That is to say, the great Elixirs, both Red and White <note>In alchemy, the "White Elixir" was believed to transmute base metals into silver, while the "Red Elixir" (or Philosopher's Stone) turned them into gold.</note>.

For may it please you to trust that I have truly found
The perfect way of the most secret Alchemy,
Which I will never truly make public for Mark nor for Pound <note>original: "Merke ne for Pounde"; types of currency, meaning he will not sell the secret for any amount of money</note>,
Except to you, and that conditionally:
That you shall keep it entirely secret yourself,
And only use it as it may be for God's pleasure;
Otherwise, in time to come, I would suffer <note>original: "abye"; to pay the penalty or endure the consequences of an action</note> God's judgment
For my revealing of His secret treasure.

Therefore, consider carefully with good deliberation,
For no other creature shall know of this secret
But you alone, as I make this faithful declaration,
For as long as I remain in this life:
To which I desire your Lordship to assure me,
And to agree to my desire in this by oath,
Lest I should bring the wrath of God upon myself
By revealing His great gift and secret <note>original: "previtie"; a private matter or a divine mystery</note>.

And yet, moreover, I desire your Highness to pardon me,
For I will never write it openly with a pen,
But when you wish, you shall see it through practice;
Also by word of mouth, this most delightful precious secret—
How the Red and White Elixirs may be made—
Shall be clearly declared to your Highness.
And if it pleases you to help with modest expense and time <note>original: "respyte"; here likely meaning the time or opportunity needed for the long alchemical process</note>,
I will make them by the help of the Trinity.

# The Epistle

But regardless of the danger that might occur,
Although I do not dare to openly untie the knot <note>The "knot" refers to the complex riddle of the alchemical secret.</note> here,
Yet in my writing I will not be so mysterious <note>original: "Mysticall"</note>,
But that you may find the knowledge through study:
How every thing can be multiplied within its own kind,
And that the likeness of metallic bodies can be transformed <note>original: "transmutable"</note>;
I will declare that if you understand my meaning,
You shall prove my writing true and no made-up fable.

And if God allows you to gain this treasure through me,
Serve Him devoutly with more praise <note>original: "Laud"</note> and thanks,
Praying to His Godhead that you may so endure in life
As to use His gifts of grace and fortune for His pleasure;
Intending most especially above all things,
To the best of your power and skill <note>original: "connyng"</note>, to keep His ten commandments <note>original: "precepts tenne"</note>
So that you bring yourself into no danger;
But that you may see Him in glory hereafter, Amen.

As the Philosopher <note>Ripley is referring to Aristotle, often called "The Philosopher" in medieval texts.</note> writes in the book of *Meteors* <note>original: "boke of Meteors"; referring to Aristotle's *Meteorologica*, a foundational text for medieval alchemy and science.</note>,
The likeness of metallic bodies cannot be transformed;
But afterward he added these more delightful words:
"Unless they are reduced to their original material state."
Therefore, such bodies which are naturally meltable <note>original: "liquable"</note>,
Both mineral and metallic, may be converted into a mercurial state <note>original: "Mercurizate"</note>;
You may understand that this science is not a matter of mere opinion,
But determined to be very true by Raymond <note>original: "Raymond"; likely Ramon Llull (c. 1232–1315), a philosopher whose name was frequently attached to alchemical works.</note> and others.

In the same book, the Philosopher also speaks—
If it pleases your Highness to read it there—
Of various sulphurs, but especially of two,
And of two mercuries joined to them indeed;
By which he leads those with true understanding
To the knowledge of the principles which are true:
Both the most pure Red and the White [elixirs], as I have succeeded in finding <note>original: "spede"</note>,
Which are, nevertheless, found by very few people.

<summary>George Ripley explains that metals can be transformed if they are returned to their base liquid state, citing Aristotle and Ramon Llull as authorities. He urges the King to use this alchemical knowledge for God’s glory and to keep the Ten Commandments.</summary>

<keywords>transmutation, Aristotle, Ramon Llull, mercury, sulphur, metallic bodies, Red and White Elixirs, alchemy theory</keywords>

# The Epistle.

*And these two things he quickly adds are best* <note>original: "anone"</note>
*For those who practice alchemy to use,*
*To make our Gold and our Silver therewith alone;*
*Therefore I say, whoever wishes to make our Pearl and Ruby,*
*Let him see that he does not forsake the said principles:*
*For if his principles are true at the beginning,*
*And if he can bake them so by his craft;*
*Truly, at the end, he shall not regret* <note>original: "rewe"</note> *his work.*

*But one great secret is very necessary to know,*
*That though the Philosophers speak plurally,*
*It is all but one Thing, you may believe me,* <note>original: "trowe"</note>
*In nature,* <note>original: "kinde"</note> *which is principally our Base material,*
*From which both the White and the Red spring naturally;* <note>The "White" and "Red" refer to the *albedo* (whitening) and *rubedo* (reddening) stages of the alchemical Great Work, which were said to produce silver and gold.</note>
*And yet the White must come before the Red:*
*Which thing is not wrought by hand,*
*But naturally, with Craft helping it out of our Lead.* <note>Alchemists believed that "Philosophical Lead" was the starting material for the Stone.</note>

*For all the parts of our most precious Stone,*
*As I can prove, are co-essential and concrete;*
*Moreover, there is no true principle but one;*
*It was a very long time before I could find it:*
*He who can reduce it, and knows its Heat,*
*And can only correct nature with its own nature,* <note>original: "kinde with kinde"</note>
*Until original filth is cleansed from its seat,*
*Is likely to find our secrets, both great and small.*

*Therefore, only work Nature with its own Nature,*
*And join all your Elements so that they do not strive;*
*Bear this point in mind above all things:*
*That you turn passive natures into active ones,*
*Of Water, Fire, and Wind, and of Earth, make them move quickly;* <note>original: "blive"</note>
*And of the Quadrangle, make a round Figure;* <note>A reference to "squaring the circle," a symbol for the union of the four elements and the creation of the Philosopher’s Stone.</note>
*Then you shall have honey from our beehive;*
*One ounce of which is well worth a thousand pounds.*

<meta>catchword: The</meta>

<summary>This page outlines the core alchemical principle that the "Great Work" relies on a single underlying substance and the natural harmony of elements. The author emphasizes that the "White" and "Red" stages (silver and gold) come from the same source through the "squaring of the circle."</summary>

# The Epistle.

*The principal secret of all secrets*
*Is true Proportion, which must not be forgotten,*
*Wherein I counsel you, do not be superficial,*
*If you ever expect to find the true conclusion;*
*Turn Earth to Water, and Water into Wind,* <note>Wind here refers to the element of Air.</note>
*From that make Fire, and beware of the Flood*
*Of Noah, in which many a person is blinded;* <note>In alchemy, the "Flood of Noah" refers to an excess of liquid solvent that "drowns" the substance, ruining the experiment.</note>
*So that by this science they gain but little good.*

*I counsel you to eat and drink temperately,*
*And be very careful that Hyposarca* <term>original: "Iposarcha" — a medical term for a type of dropsy or swelling caused by fluid under the skin.</term> *does not take hold;*
*Do not weaken* <note>original: "Nesh"</note> *your belly by drinking immoderately,*
*Lest you quench your natural heat in a short time;*
*The color appearing in your face will tell the tale:*
*Drink no more, therefore, than you can eat;*
*Walk up and down at an easy pace,*
*Do not drive your body too hard so as to sweat.*

*With a gentle fire after moving, if you sweat,*
*Warm your body and make it dry again;*
*Walk by rivers and fountains after meals:*
*Early in the morning, visit the high mountains,*
*For Medicine* <note>original: "Physick"</note> *surely commands that, as I read:*
*Nevertheless, do not ascend the mountain so high*
*That you cannot have a clear path downward,*
*And defend yourself from the cold with your cloak.* <note>original: "Mantell"</note>

*Such labor is healthy, if you will dry your sweat*
*With a napkin, and after it take no cold,*
*For thick* <note>original: "groſe"</note> *humors are naturally purged by sweat;*
*Use Diacameron,* <note>An alchemical or medicinal confection/paste.</note> *then prepared with perfect Gold;*
*I hold Hermodactyl* <note>original: "Hermodactilus" — a plant used to treat joint pain and gout.</note> *to be good for watery humors,*
*Use Perforated St. John's Wort* <note>original: "Hipericon Perforate"</note> *with the milk of Spurge;* <note>original: "Tithimall"</note>
*And Spermaceti in equal parts* <note>original: "ana" — a medical abbreviation for equal parts of each ingredient.</note> *with red wine when you grow old,*
*And goat's milk boiled* <note>original: "sodden"</note> *with Gold nourishes the radical moisture.* <note>The "radical moisture" was thought to be the essential life-sustaining fluid within the body.</note>

<summary>This page outlines the importance of balancing the four elements (Earth, Water, Air, Fire) and provides a health regimen for the alchemist, including dietary moderation, exercise, and medicinal recipes involving gold and herbs.</summary>

# The Epistle.

But whoever intends to be a good physician
Needs to know our "lower astronomy" <note>original: "lower Astronomy" — a term for alchemy, which studies the "stars" or essential spirits within earthly matter, mirroring the stars in the sky.</note> well.
After that, he must learn to examine urine well in a glass,
And if it needs to be heated <note>original: "chased"</note>, he must blow the fire.
Then, he must cleverly process it in various ways,
And after finding the cause, create a pleasant <note>original: "blithe"</note> medicine,
Accurately identifying all the illnesses in a row;
Whoever can do this through his medical skill <note>original: "Physicke"</note> is likely to thrive.

We have an incorruptible heaven made of the Quintessence,
Adorned with bright elements, signs, planets, and stars,
Which moistens our Earth by subtle influence;
And out of that Earth, it draws <note>original: "fetteth"</note> a secret sulphur hidden from sight
By the power of its attractive might,
Just as the bee gathers honey out of the flower—
A thing no other earthly being <note>original: "wight"</note> can do;
Therefore, let glory and honor be to God alone.

And just as ice melts <note>original: "relente"</note> into water—
From which it was congealed by the force of great cold—
When Phoebus <note>The sun, representing heat.</note> strikes it with his flowing heat,
Just so, our gold is reduced to "mineral water"
(As Albert, Raymond, and Arnold <note>Albertus Magnus, Raymond Lully, and Arnold of Villanova: three of the most influential medieval authorities on alchemy.</note> plainly write)
With heat and moisture brought about <note>original: "occafionate"</note> by our craft,
Along with the thickening <note>original: "congelation"</note> of the spirit. Look! Now I have told you
How our materials must be balanced <note>original: "proportionate"</note> together.

You may learn this science from the dyer's craft,
By observing how they make decoctions <note>Extractions made by boiling substances to remove their essence.</note> with water
Using their woad <note>original: "Woñd" — a plant used to produce blue dye.</note> and madder <note>A plant used to produce red dye.</note> easily and with patience,
Until the dyes <note>original: "Tinctures"</note> appear, which the cloth then takes.
They are so fixed within it that they will never leave
The cloth when washed, after they are joined;
Just so, we draw our tinctures with the "Water of our Lake,"
By boiling them with the "Ashes of Hermes' tree." <note>A symbolic alchemical term referring to the processed residue of the "Great Work," named for Hermes Trismegistus, the mythical founder of alchemy.</note>

<summary>The author compares the practice of alchemy to the diagnostic skills of a physician, the natural extraction of honey by bees, and the industrial process of dyeing cloth to explain how "tinctures" are extracted and fixed.</summary>
<keywords>alchemy, medicine, physician, woad, madder, tincture, Quintessence, Hermes Trismegistus, Albertus Magnus, Raymond Lully, Arnold of Villanova</keywords>

<meta>This page continues the "Epistle," moving from the theoretical foundations of alchemy to a poetic description of the practical laboratory stages and the symbolic "bestiary" of chemical transformations.</meta>

# The Epistle.

When these tinctures are made perfect through the craft,
They dye metals with colors that are forever permanent,
Depending on the quality of the medicine—whether Red or White <note>The "White" medicine (lunar) turns base metals to silver; the "Red" (solar) turns them to gold.</note>;
So that they will never be burned away by any fire.
If you pay close attention <note>original: "take good tent"</note> to this example,
You shall achieve your purpose all the sooner;
And ensure your fire is gentle and not intense;
Observe where Nature left off, for that is when you must begin.

First calcine <note>original: "Calcine" — to heat a substance until it reduces to powder.</note>, and after that putrefy,
Dissolve, distill, sublime, descend, and fix,
With *aqua vitae* <note>original: "Aquavite" — literally "water of life," referring to a potent solvent or distilled spirit.</note> wash and dry it many times,
And create a marriage between the Body and the Spirit;
If you can naturally mix these together in this way,
By dissolving the Body, the water shall become congealed,
Then the Body shall die completely of the flux <note>original: "Flixe" — here referring to a flowing or softening state of the material during chemical breakdown.</note>,
Bleeding and changing colors, as you shall witness.

On the third day, he shall rise to life again,
And devour birds and beasts of the wilderness:
Crows, parrots <note>original: "Popingayes"</note>, magpies <note>original: "Pyes"</note>, peacocks, and song thrushes <note>original: "Mavies"</note>;
The Phoenix, the white Eagle, and the fearsome Griffin,
He shall conquer <note>original: "destres"</note> the Green Lion and the Red Dragon,
The white Dragon also, the antelope, the unicorn, and the panther,
Along with other birds and beasts, both great and small;
Even the Basilisk, which almost everyone fears.

In *Bus* and *Nubi* <note>Obscure alchemical terms likely referring to the "hidden" and "cloudy" stages of the matter.</note> he shall rise and ascend,
Up to the Moon, and then <note>original: "sith"</note> up to the Sun,
Through the Ocean Sea, which is a circle without end:
Sailing only within a small glass vessel <note>original: "glasen Tonne"</note>,
When he arrives there, then the Mastery is won.
You will not need to spend great wealth on this journey,
And yet you shall be glad that it was ever begun,
If you choose to attend to your work with patience.

# The Epistle

For then both **Body** and **Spirit**, and also both **Oil** and **Water**,
**Soul** and **Tincture** are one thing, both **White** and **Red**.
Through changing **Colors**, it contains whatever men may chatter about;
It is also called this once it has been **Dead**
And is revived: our **Marcasite**, our **Magnet**, and our **Lead**,
Our **Sulphur**, our **Arsenic**, and our true **Quicklime** <term>Calcevive: unslaked lime (calcium oxide), used in alchemy as a caustic agent for "burning" or transforming substances</term>;
Our **Sun**, our **Moon**, the **Ferment** of our **Bread**,
Our **Toad**, our **Basilisk**, our unknown **Body**, our **Man**,
and our **Wife**.

When our **Body** is naturally renovated by this craft,
It is called a **Medicine** of the first order in our philosophy,
Which must often be **spiritualized** <note>original: "Spiritualizate"</note> again,
Turning the round **Wheel** of our aforementioned **astronomy** <note>Alchemists used "astronomy" and "planets" to describe the cyclic movements and chemical properties of their materials.</note>.
And so you must come to the **Elixir** of **Spirits**, because
Until the fixed part is overcome by the "flyer" <term>flier: a volatile substance that evaporates or sublimes easily, as opposed to "fixed" substances that resist heat</term>,
It is only named the **Elixir** of **Bodies**;
And this secret point truly deceives many people.

This natural process, completed by the help of craft,
Dissolves the spiritual **Elixir** in our oily **Moisture**.
Then let them be **circulated** together in **Mary’s Bath** <term>Balneo of Mary: a water bath or bain-marie, providing gentle, indirect heat for distillation or digestion</term>,
Until they are perfectly thickened like new **Honey** or **Oil**.
Then that **Medicine** will heal every kind of **infirmity**
And turn all **Metals** most perfectly to the **Sun** and **Moon** <note>original: "Sonne & Moone," meaning Gold and Silver</note>.
Thus shall you have both the great **Elixir** and **Drinkable Gold** <note>original: "Aurum Potabile," a legendary medicinal liquid made from gold, believed to grant longevity</note>,
By the grace and will of **God**, to whom be praise eternally.

The Moon, which is called the lesser Lunary <note>original: Lunary; often a symbolic name for silver or the feminine principle in alchemy</note>,

# *The Theory Begins* <note>Latin: Incipit Theorica</note>

We intend now, through divine grace,
To write a few words concerning Chaos <note>the "Prima Materia" or the unformed first matter of the universe</note>;
To cause light to shine forth from darkness,
Long hidden before, as I shall relate.
In every unknown thing, it is necessary
To search out a secret that is invisible—
The material of our mastery, an imperceptible <note>original: insensible</note> substance.

2. Because I should not seem to keep to myself 
The long-hidden secrets committed to me 
By my Lord God, I will therefore speak plainly of *Chaos*. 
My purpose shall be to fulfill my duty <note>original: "be thereof to be acquitted," meaning to be released from the obligation of keeping the secret</note> regarding it, 
For heavy burdens are not easily lightened. 
In faith, therefore, I shall endeavor 
To honorably discharge my duty before God forever.

3. Devoutly, therefore, I call unto you, O Lord; 
Send me your *Grace* to explain 
*Chaos*. For you are the opener of all secrets, 
And are ever ready to hear the supplication 
Of your humble servants. With heartfelt humility, 
I apply myself to you: send me now your grace 
Regarding your secrets, to write of them in the proper order, time, and place.

4. *Chaos* means nothing more than this, without doubt 
(As *Ovid* writes in his *Metamorphoses*): 
A certain crude substance, an unordered mass <note>original: "indigestaque moles," a Latin phrase from Ovid describing the universe before the elements were separated</note>, 
Having various natures resting within it, 
Which we may extract <note>original: "twyne," meaning to separate or pull out</note> by using their opposites. 
By the *Philosopher's Art* <term>Alchemy</term>, whoever knows the method <note>original: "seat"</note> 
May draw the four elements out from *Chaos*.

5. This *Chaos*, like all things, has three dimensions, 
Which, if well considered, shall produce the result; 
That is, *Height, Width,* and *Depth* <note>original: "Altitude, Latitude and Profunditie"</note>. 
By these three, all the "Water" <note>In alchemy, "Water" often refers to the prime matter or the universal solvent</note> is directed. 
Whoever has no respect for these dimensions 
Shall never divide the *Chaos* according to its kind, 
But after all his labor, he shall find only failure <note>original: "fraud"</note> in the end.

6. *Chaos* is to us the grapevine, both white and red; 
*Chaos* is every beast, fish, and fowl of every kind; 
*Chaos* is the ore and the mine of tin and lead, 
Of gold and silver that we find, 
And of iron and copper—things which bind us. 
They hold our sight and our wits bound to them, 
Yet we do not understand the secrets hidden within them.

Child of this discipline <term>discipline</term> <note>In this context, "discipline" refers to the specific field of alchemical and philosophical study</note>, incline your ear to me,

All manner of good things shall come with them,

1. We have sufficiently declared the *Theory*,
Making the declaration in mystical words.
Let us now proceed plainly with the *Practice*,
To give a full explanation of the Matter.
I desire, therefore, that you take good note of my narration,

I commend my *Testament* and last *Will* to you.

Overcome Satan, and see that you seek God's glory.

Always keep the fatherless and the widow in your mind.
Love the innocent as brothers; avoid the wicked.
Let falsehood and flattery go, lest you regret it.

# The Preface.

And for as much as we have for your sake
Renounced the world, our wills, and the fleshly lust,
Accept us as your own willing professors <note>original: "wylfull professyors"; those who have taken religious vows or dedicated themselves to the study of the Art</note>;

I present myself as one with humble submission,

In the order of Canon Regular of Bridlington <note>Bridlington Priory in Yorkshire; George Ripley (c. 1415–1490) was a famous English alchemist and Augustinian canon</note>;
Beseeching the Lord that you will spare me,
To declare your secrets to your true servants.

In the beginning when you made all from nothing,
A globose <note>spherical or shapeless</note> matter, dark and in confusion,
Was marvelously wrought by you, the Beginner,
Containing naturally all things without division,
Of which you made in six days a clear distinction;
As Genesis <note>original: "Genefys"</note> openly records,
Then heaven and earth were perfected by your word.

So through your will and power, out of one confused mass
All things that have being were made;
But in your glory, you were the maker before,
Are now, and shall be without end, I know <note>original: "I wys" (ywis); an archaic term meaning certainly or indeed</note>:
And purified souls up to your bliss
Shall come. This may be one principle
For the declaring of our Stone <note>The Philosopher's Stone, the legendary substance in alchemy capable of turning base metals into gold and granting medicinal healing</note>.

<meta>This page continues "The Preface" of George Ripley's *The Compound of Alchemy*. Following the previous page’s parallel between God's creation of the world from chaos and the alchemical process, Ripley now identifies the primary substance of the "Stone" and warns against misunderstanding the true nature of alchemical mercury.</meta>

# The Preface.

For just as from one mass all things were made,
Just so must it be in our practice:
All our secrets must spring from one image.
Therefore, in *philosophers’* books, whoever wishes to see,
Our *Stone* is called the "lesser world," <note>original: "the leſſe World"; also known as the microcosm, reflecting the idea that the human or the Stone contains the universe within itself</note> one and three,
Also *magnesia* <note>original: "Magneſia"; in alchemy, this refers to the "primal matter" or the "mother" of the stone, not the modern chemical magnesium</note> consisting of *sulfur* and *mercury*,
Proportioned by nature most perfectly.

But many a person marvels—as well they might—
And muses on such a marvelous thing:
"What is our *Stone*?" since *philosophers* say
To those who are forever seeking it:
"Yet birds and fish bring it to us;
Every single person has it, and it is in every place,
In you, in me, in every time and space."

To this I answer: it is *mercury*, I know <note>original: "I wys" (ywis); certainly or indeed</note>,
But not the common kind called *quicksilver* by name,
But the *mercury* without which nothing has being;
All true *philosophers* record and say the same.
But simple seekers find fault with them,
Saying they hid the truth; but they themselves are blameworthy,
Who are not *scholars* <note>original: "Clerks"; educated persons or clerics capable of reading Latin</note> and yet meddle with *philosophy* <note>original: "Phyloſophy"; here meaning alchemy, the "Hermetic Philosophy"</note>.

But though it is *mercury*, yet understand this wisely:
Where it is, and where you should seek it;
Otherwise, I counsel you not to take this work in hand,
For *philosophers* flatter fools with fair speech.
But listen to me, for truly I will teach you
Which is your most profitable *mercury*,
Being in no way deceptive to you.

He warns that the Stone is omnipresent but hidden by the deceptive language of past philosophers, which only true scholars can decode.</summary>

<meta>This page continues "The Preface" of George Ripley's *The Compound of Alchemy*. Having established that the "Stone" is found everywhere in nature, Ripley now moves to clarify the specific nature of alchemical *mercury* and the "three mercuries" or "menstrues" necessary for the work.</meta>

# The Preface.

It is more near <note>original: "nythe" (nigh); meaning the truth is more accessible or intrinsic in certain substances than others</note> in some things than in others,
Therefore take heed <note>original: "tent"; attention or heed</note> to what I write to you,
For if you never come to the knowledge
Of it, yet you shall not reproach <note>original: "twytt"; to twit, blame, or find fault with</note> me:
For I will truly now urge <note>original: "excite"; to stir up or encourage</note> you,
To understand well the three *Mercuries*,
Which are the keys of our *Science* <note>original: "Scyens"; the "Sacred Science" of alchemy</note>.

*Raymond* <note>Raymond Lully (c. 1232–1315), a famous philosopher and reputed alchemist to whom many works were attributed</note> calls them his "Menstrues" <note>original: "Menstrues"; in alchemy, a solvent or "mother-liquid" that dissolves and transforms the material</note>,
Without which truly no truth is achieved,
But two of them are superficial:
The third is essential, consisting of the *Sun* <note>original: "Soon"; gold</note> and *Moon* <note>original: "Moone"; silver</note>;
Their properties I will declare very soon,
And the *Mercury* essential to other metals
Is the principal of our material *Stone*.

In the *Sun* and *Moon* our "Menstrue" is not seen;
It does not appear except by its effect on the sight,
That is the *Stone* of which we mean;
Whoever understands our writing correctly, [will see]
It is a Soul, a bright substance:
A subtle influence of the *Sun* and *Moon*,
By which the Earth receives brilliance.

For what are *Gold* and *Silver*, says *Avicenna* <note>Ibn Sina (c. 980–1037), the Persian polymath whose medical and philosophical texts were central to medieval alchemy</note>,
But Earth which is pure White and Red?
Take from that the said clarity, and then
That Earth will be of little use;
The whole compound is called our *Lead* <note>The "Lead of the Philosophers," a raw, unrefined state of the matter, not common plumbing lead</note>,
The quality of clarity comes from the *Sun* and *Moon*;
These are our "Menstrues," one and all.

<meta>catchword: Bodies</meta>

# The Preface.

Bodies with the first we **calcine** <note>original: "calcene"; to reduce a substance to powder or ash by heat, a primary alchemical process of purification.</note> naturally
As perfect, but none which are unclean,
Except one which is usually
Named by philosophers the **Green Lion**; <note>A common alchemical symbol often representing raw mineral ore (like antimony or vitriol) or a powerful acidic solvent used to dissolve gold.</note>
He is the middle ground between the **Sun and Moon**: <note>In alchemy, the "Sun" usually represents gold and the "Moon" represents silver.</note>
Of joining tinctures with perfection,
As **Geber** <note>Jabir ibn Hayyan (c. 721–c. 815), a legendary Arabic alchemist whose works were foundational to European alchemy.</note> testifies.

With the second, which is a living <note>original: "Vegetable"; in alchemy, this refers to the life-force or "growing" potential of the substance rather than literal plants.</note> moisture
Reviving that which was formerly dead,
Both material principles must be loosened
And formal ones, or else they are of little use:
Therefore, know the **solvents** <note>original: "Menstrues"; from the Latin *menstruum*, these are powerful liquids used to dissolve solids, often compared to the biological cycle in their role of "nourishing" the philosophical child or Stone.</note> I advise:
Without which neither true calcination
Can be done, nor yet natural dissolution.

With the third moisture, most permanent,
Incombustible and oily in its nature,
The **Tree of Hermes** <note>A symbol for the alchemical process or the growth of the "Great Work."</note> must be burned to ashes:
It is our natural fire most sure,
Our **mercury**, or **sulphur**, or pure tincture:
Our **Soul**, our **Stone**, borne up with wind,
Engendered in the Earth; keep this in your mind. <note>These lines allude to the *Emerald Tablet of Hermes Trismegistus*, which says of the Stone: "The wind carried it in its belly, the earth is its nurse."</note>

This Stone also, I dare tell you,
Is the potential vapor of metals;
How you shall get it, you must be careful,
For truly this solvent <note>original: "Menstruall"</note> is invisible:
However, with the second **philosophical water**,
By separation of elements it may appear
To the sight in the form of clear water.

# The Preface.

From our solvent <note>original: "Menstrue"; a powerful liquid used to dissolve solids.</note> made abundant <note>original: "exuberate"</note> by labor,
The *Sulphur* of nature may be made with it.
If it be well and naturally <note>original: "kyndly"</note> sharpened <note>original: "acuate"; made potent or acidic.</note>,
And circulated into a pure Spirit:
Then you must be sure to dissolve
Your Base <note>The solid material being worked upon.</note> with it in various ways,
As you shall know by your practice.

That point, therefore, in its due place,
I will declare along with many others,
If God will grant me time <note>original: "space"</note> and grace,
And keep <note>original: "reserve"</note> me alive and free from woe;
Make sure you do exactly as I teach you,
And for your first principal foundation,
Understand your menstrual water <note>The primary alchemical solvent.</note>.

And when you have performed true **Calcination**, <note>The process of heating a substance until it is reduced to a fine powder.</note>
Increasing and not wasting the **radical moisture**, <note>original: "moysture radycall"; the essential, life-sustaining fluid believed to exist within all matter.</note>
Until your Base, by frequent refinement <note>original: "subtylyatyon"</note>,
Will flow as easily as wax upon metal;
Then loosen it with your living <note>original: "vegetable"; refers to the life-giving or "growing" property of the substance.</note> solvent,
Until you have oil from it, bright in color,
Then is your solvent visible to the sight.

And oil is drawn out in the color of gold,
Or something like it, out of our fine **Red Lead**, <note>In alchemy, "Red Lead" often refers to a specific state of the matter (like lead tetroxide) or a symbolic stage in the process.</note>
Which *Raymond* <note>Raymond Lully (c. 1232–1315), a famous philosopher and alchemist.</note> said when he was old,
Would serve him much better than gold;
For when he was near death from old age,
He made from it **drinkable gold**, <note>original: *Aurum Potabile*; a legendary alchemical medicine believed to grant longevity and cure all diseases.</note>
Which revived him, as people could see.

# The Preface.

For they may be circulated together in this way,
That is to say, the Oil and the vegetable Menstrual <note>original: "Menstruall"; a powerful alchemical solvent.</note>,
Either made abundant <note>original: "exuberate"</note> through labor,
And made by Craft a Celestial Stone:
Of a nature so fiery that we call it
Our *Basilisk*, otherwise our *Cockatrice*,
Our great *Elixir* of the highest value <note>original: "pryse".</note>.

Which, just as the sight of a *Basilisk*
Kills its object, so it slays crude *Mercury*
When it is projected upon it,
In the blink of an eye, most suddenly,
So that the *Mercury* is fixed <note>original: "teynyth"; meaning stained or permanently transformed/solidified.</note> permanently;
Turning all metallic bodies into perfect *Sun* <note>Gold</note> and *Moon* <note>Silver</note>,
Thus guide your base material to become both Red and White.

*Potable Gold* <note>original: "Aurum potabile"; a legendary medicine made of liquid gold.</note> is made in this way,
From Gold, though not the common calcined kind;
But from our *Tincture* which will not fade,
Drawn out of our Base with the circulated Menstrual solvent.
But natural **Calcination** <note>The process of heating a substance until it is reduced to a fine powder.</note> must always
Be performed before your Gold can be dissolved;
That first Principle I will tell you now.

But I shall divide this Treatise into Chapters,
Twelve in number, with a proper recapitulation;
I lay aside superfluous repetitions,
Intending only to give true information,
Both of the theoretical and practical operation:
So that whoever chooses to be guided by my writing
Shall succeed perfectly in his intent.

# The Preface.

The first chapter shall be about natural *Calcination* <note>The process of heating a substance to a high temperature to reduce it to a fine powder.</note>;
The second of secret and *Philosophical* *Dissolution*;
The third of our *Elemental Separation*;
The fourth of matrimonial *Conjunction* <note>The chemical joining of substances, often described as a "marriage" between the Sun (Gold) and Moon (Silver).</note>;
The fifth of *Putrefaction* <note>The stage of decomposition and blackening, often called "the crow's head."</note> shall then follow;
Of *Congelation* <note>Solidifying or thickening the matter.</note>, the whitening <note>original: "albyfycative"</note> shall be the sixth,
Then of *Cibation* <note>The process of "feeding" the material with fresh liquid to sustain it.</note> the seventh shall follow next.

The secret of our *Sublimation* the eighth shall show;
The ninth shall be of *Fermentation*,
The tenth of our *Exaltation* <note>Raising the potency and purity of the chemical substance.</note>, I believe <note>original: "trow"</note>;
The eleventh of our marvelous *Multiplication* <note>Increasing the quantity and power of the Alchemical Elixir.</note>;
The twelfth of *Projection* <note>The final stage, where the finished Elixir is cast upon base metal to transform it into gold.</note>; then *Recapitulation*;
And so this Treatise shall come to an end,
By the help of God, as I intend.

# OF CALCINATION.

## *The First Gate.*

<margin>1.</margin>
Calcination is the purification <note>original: "purgacyon"</note> of our *Stone*,
Restoring also its natural heat;
Of radical moisture it loses none;
Inducing a most suitable Solution into our *Stone*,
According to *Philosophy*, I promise you <note>original: "behyte"; I promise or assure you.</note>,
->Do not do it according to the common manner <note>original: "comyn gyse"</note>,<-
->With Sulphur and Salts prepared in various ways.<-

<margin>2.</margin>
Neither with corrosives nor with fire alone,
Nor with vinegar nor "ardent water" <note>original: "water ardent"; literally "burning water," usually referring to distilled alcohol or a strong acid.</note>,
Neither with the vapor of lead is our *Stone*
Calcined for our purpose:
All those who are determined to calcine in such a way,
->Should withdraw their hand from this difficult *Science*,<-
->Until they understand our *Calcining* better.<-

<margin>3.</margin>
For by such calcining their bodies are ruined <note>original: "shent"</note>,
Which diminishes the moisture of our *Stone*;
Therefore, when bodies are burned to powder,
Dry as the ashes of wood <note>original: "Tre"</note> or bone,
We want nothing to do with such a *Calx* <note>original: "Calx"; the powdery substance remaining after a metal or mineral has been thoroughly heated or burned.</note>,
->For we multiply radical moisture <note>The innate, essential "life-liquid" within a substance according to alchemical theory.</note>,<-
->In Calcining, diminishing none at all.<-

> And for a sure foundation of our true ***Calcination***,
> Work wisely nature <note>original: "kynde"; referring to the natural essence or "like" substances.</note> only with nature;
> For nature has a natural inclination toward its own kind;
> He who does not know this is but blind in his knowledge:

> ->Everything is first calcined in its own kind,<-
> ->By understanding this well, you shall find success therein.<-

> By a very long process, as ***Philosophers*** write,

> ->Able to be stained with a color which will not fade.<-

> Let the body <note>the solid metal, such as gold or silver.</note> be subtly filed,
> With as much Mercury as is then refined <note>original: "subtylyd".</note>:
> ->One part of the Sun <note>Gold</note>, two of the Moon <note>Silver</note>,<-

# OF CALCINATION.

<margin>12.</margin>
Behold how that loom <note>the alchemical vessel or furnace</note> is tempered,
And also the method by which you calcine it;
And always look to keep this in mind,
That your Earth <note>the solid matter or "body"</note> is never suffocated by Water <note>the solvent or mercury</note>.
Dry up your moisture with heat most temperate:
   Help dissolution with the moisture of the Moon <note>silver or the "lunar" cool moisture</note>,
   And solidification <note>original: "Congellacyon"</note> with the Sun <note>gold or the "solar" heat</note>, then you have finished.

<margin>13.</margin>
Four natures shall thus turn into the fifth <note>the quintessence, the perfect balance of elements</note>,
Which is a nature most perfect and temperate;
But it is hard to kick with your bare foot
Against a broad spike <note>original: "brodyke"; a spike or goad</note> of iron or newly sharpened <note>original: "acuate"</note> steel.
So many do who are infatuated <note>foolish or deluded</note>,
   When they take such high things in hand,
   Which they do not understand in any way.

<margin>14.</margin>
In eggs, in vitriol <note>sulfuric acid or metallic sulfates</note>, or in blood,
What riches do they think <note>original: "wene"</note> they will find there?
If they understood Philosophy <note>the "True Philosophy" of alchemy</note>,
They would not be so blind in their working,
Seeking to find gold or silver out of their own kind <note>from non-metallic substances</note>:
   For just as fire is the principle of burning,
   So gold is certainly <note>original: "I wys"</note> the principle of making gold.

<margin>15.</margin>
If you intend, therefore, to make
Gold and silver by the craft of our *Philosophy*;
Do not take eggs or blood for it,
But use gold and silver which, naturally and
Wisely calcined (and not just by manual labor),
   Will bring forth a new generation,
   Increasing their own kind as does every living thing.

16. &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;And if it were true that perfection could be found
In things which are not metallic <term>mettallyne: made of or containing metal</term>:
In which there are colors pleasant to see,
As in blood, eggs, hair, urine, and wine,
Or in base metals dug out of the mine;
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Yet their elements must be putrefied <term>putrefyed: decomposed or broken down chemically</term> and separated,
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;And be wedded <note>original: "dyſponſate"; to be betrothed or joined in marriage</note> with the elements of perfect bodies <note>gold and silver</note>.

17. &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;But first, make a rotation of these elements,
And turn your Earth into Water first of all;
Then from your Water make Air by levigation <term>Levygacyon: the process of grinding a substance into a fine powder or reducing it to a light, airy state</term>;
And make Air into Fire; then **MASTER** I will call you
Of all our secrets great and small:
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;If you can turn the Wheel of Elements about,
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Truly understanding our writings without doubt.

18. &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;This done, go backward, turning your wheel again,
And then turn your Fire into Water at once;
And Air into Earth, or else you labor only in vain:
For in this way our *Stone* is brought to the right temperament <note>the balanced state of the four qualities</note>,
And four contrary natures are made into one,
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;After they have been cycled three times,
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;And also your base <note>the foundation of the work</note> is perfectly completed.

19. &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Thus, under the moisture of the *Moon* <note>silver or cool, moist energy</note>,
And under the temperate heat of the *Sun* <note>gold or warm, dry energy</note>,
Your elements shall soon be incinerated <term>incynerate: reduced to ashes through calcination</term>,
And then you have won the mastery;
Thank God your work was then begun:
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;For there you have one true sign,
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Which will first show itself to you in blackness <note>the Nigredo stage, signifying the "death" of the old forms before they can be purified and reborn</note>.

# OF SOLUTION.

## The second Gate.

<margin>1.</margin>
Of Solution now will I speak a word or two,
Which shows what was before hidden from sight,
And also thins things that were thick;
By the virtue of our first Menstruum <note>original: "Menstrue"; a solvent used in alchemy to dissolve solids</note> clear and bright,
In which our Bodies are eclipsed to the sight:
And from their hard and dry compaction subtilized <term>subtilized: refined or made thinner and less dense</term>
Into their own first nature naturally returned <note>original: "retrograde"; reverting to an earlier, more primal state</note>.

<margin>2.</margin>
One in gender they are, and in number not so,
Whose Father is the Sun, and the Moon truly is the Mother;
The mediator <note>original: "mean"</note> is Mercury; these two and no more
Are our Magnesia <note>original: "Magnesia"; a term for the primary material of the Great Work</note>, our Adrop <note>original: "Adrop"; a symbolic name for the "body" or crude lead before purification</note>, and none other;
There are things, but only as Sister and Brother:
That is to say, Agent and Patient,
Sulphur and Mercury, both essential to our intent.

<margin>3.</margin>
Between these two in contrary qualities,
A mediator is engendered most marvelously,
Which is our Mercury and oily Menstruum <note>original: "Menstrue unctuose"</note>;
Our secret Sulphur working invisibly,
Burning the body more fiercely than fire,
Dissolving the mineral body into water,
Which we call "Night from darkness" in the North part <note>The "North part" refers to the cold, dark stage of the work, often associated with the element of water and the black color of the Nigredo</note>.

# Of Solution.

4. But yet I believe you do not fully understand
The true secret of the Philosophers' *Dissolution*;
Therefore, listen to me—I advise you wisely:
For I will tell you truly, without any deception;
Our *Solution* is the cause of our *Congelation* <term>congelation: the process of thickening or solidifying a liquid</term>;
For the *Dissolution* of the physical body on one side
Causes *Congelation* of the spiritual on the other.

5. And we dissolve into "water which does not wet the hand" <note>original: "Water whych weytyth no hond"; a common alchemical paradox referring to a corrosive or philosophical solvent that behaves like water but is distinct from it</note>,
For when the Earth is entirely incinerated <term>incinerated: reduced to ashes through intense heat</term>;
Then the water is congealed—understand this;
For the elements are so linked together <term>concatenated: joined together as if in a chain</term>,
That when the body is altered from its first form:
A new form is immediately introduced,
For nothing can exist entirely without any form.

6. And here I will disclose a secret to you,
Which is the foundation of all our secrets;
And if you do not know it, you shall only lose
Your labor and costs, both great and small.
Take heed, therefore, so that you do not fall into error:
The more "Earth" and the less "Water" you use,
The sooner and better a *Solution* you shall see.

7. Observe how ice melts into water,
And so it must, for it was water before;
Just so, our "Earth" is turned back into water,
And the water is thereby congealed forevermore.
For according to all the Philosophers who were ever born:
Every metal was once "mineral water," <note>Alchemists believed that metals grew inside the earth from a vaporous or liquid "seed"</note>
Therefore, with water, they all turn back into water.

# OF SEPARATION.
## *The Third Gate.*

<margin>1.</margin> **S**eparation divides each part from the other,
The subtle from the gross, and the thin from the thick;
But look that you put aside manual separation: <note>The author warns against trying to separate elements physically by hand or crude tools, suggesting a more natural or chemical process.</note>
For that belongs to fools who gain little good, <note>original: "wyn"</note>
But in our *Separation*, nature does not stop: <term>blyn: to cease or stop</term>
Making a division of elemental qualities
Into the fifth degree until they are all transformed. <note>The "fifth degree" refers to the *quintessence*, the purest essence of a substance beyond the four classical elements.</note>

<margin>2.</margin> Earth is turned into water, black and blue, <note>original: "black and bloe": these colors represent the *nigredo* or blackening stage of alchemy.</note>
And water afterward into air, appearing very white:
Air is turned into fire—there are no more elements;
Of this, our *Stone* of great delight is made by craft,
But of this *Separation* we must write much more;
And *Separation* is called, by the philosophers' definition,
The fourfold dispersion <term>tetraptatyve dyfpercyon: a division into four parts (tetra-partitive)</term> of the said elements.

<margin>3.</margin> And of this *Separation*, I find a similar metaphor <note>original: "fygure"</note>
Spoken by the *Prophet* in the *Psalms*, <note>original: "Psalmody"; likely referring to Psalm 114:8 ("Who turned the rock into a standing water, the flint into a fountain of waters") or similar biblical passages where God extracts water from stone.</note>
"God brought out of a stone a flood of pure water,
And out of the hardest stone, oil abundantly":
Just so, from our precious *Stone*, if you are wise, <note>original: "wytty"</note>
You shall draw incombustible oil and water,
And for that, you do not need to blow at the coals. <note>This suggests that the true alchemical separation occurs through a natural internal heat or process, rather than the heavy, outward labor of a traditional blacksmith or "puffer."</note>

<summary>This page describes "Separation," the third gate of the alchemical process, where the four elements are divided and refined into their purest forms. # OF SEPARATION.

<margin>4.</margin> Do this with easy and measured heat,
First with moist fire, and afterward with dry;
Drawing out the phlegm <term>flewme: a watery, dull, or impure byproduct of distillation</term> with patience,
And after that, skillfully draw out your other natures.
Dry up your "earth" until it is thirsty;
Otherwise, you labor in vain by calcining, <note>Calcining is the process of heating a solid to high temperatures to remove volatile substances, often reducing it to a powder.</note>
And then make it drink up its moisture again.

<margin>5.</margin> You must perform separation in this way many times,
Dividing your matter into two parts,
So that you take the simple <note>original: "Symple"; referring to the pure, unmixed essence of a substance.</note> from the gross <note>original: "groce"; the coarse or impure parts.</note>
Until earth remains beneath, blue in color.
That earth is "fixed" <term>fyx: stable, solid, and resistant to change by fire</term> to endure all hardship;
The other part is spiritual and volatile, <note>original: "fleyng"; meaning it evaporates or rises as vapor.</note>
But you must eventually turn them both into one single thing.

<margin>6.</margin> Then Oil and Water shall distill with water,
And through its help receive refinement; <note>original: "menyng"; likely meaning "mending" or purification.</note>
Keep these two well so that you do not ruin
Your work for lack of proper sealing.
Make your stopper <term>Stopell: a plug or seal</term> of melting glass,
Joining the top of your vessel together with it;
Then it is used in the manner of the philosophers.

<margin>7.</margin> Regarding the water with which you must renew your Stone:
See that you distill it by itself many times
Before you work with it;
And by your own sight, you shall know well
When it is cleared of foul dregs. <term>feculent feces: the impure, solid sediment or waste left over from a process</term>
For some men try to multiply <term>multeply: to increase the power, quality, or quantity of the alchemical matter</term> it with Saturn, <note>Saturn is the alchemical name for the metal lead.</note>
And other substances which we reject. <note>original: "defye"; to renounce or refuse to use.</note>

# OF CONJUNCTION.
## *The Fourth Gate.*

<margin>1.</margin> After the chapter on natural separation,
By which the elements of our Stone <note>The "Philosopher’s Stone," the final perfected substance of the alchemical work.</note> were divided,
There follows here the chapter on secret conjunction.
This process joins opposing natures into perfect unity,
And knits them together so that none may flee from the others;
When they are tested <note>original: "examynate"; to be examined or tested, usually by fire in a crucible.</note> by fire,
They shall be securely joined <note>original: "conjugate"; united as a pair.</note> together.

<margin>2.</margin> And therefore philosophers give this definition,
Saying that "conjunction" is nothing else
But a coupling <note>original: "copulacyon"; a union or joining.</note> of separated qualities;
Or, as others say, an equalization <note>original: "coequacyon"; the balancing of different principles in equal proportion.</note> of principles.
But some people, using the mercury that apothecaries <note>original: "Potecarys"; pharmacists. Ripley warns against using common "quicksilver" bought in a shop rather than the specialized "mercury" prepared by an alchemist.</note> sell,
Mix "bodies" <note>In alchemy, metals were often referred to as "bodies."</note> which cannot divide
Their matter, and therefore they go astray.

<margin>3.</margin> For until the time the soul is separated
And cleansed from its original sin <note>Ripley uses "original sin" as a metaphor for the natural impurities found in raw metallic ores.</note>
With the water, and purely spiritualized,
You can never begin your true conjunction.
Therefore, first separate <note>original: "twyn"; to part or divide.</note> the soul from the body;
Then, between the physical part and the spiritual part,
The soul shall cause a perpetual conjunction.

<summary>This page introduces "Conjunction," the fourth stage of the alchemical process, where previously separated elements are reunited. Ripley defines this as a balancing of principles and warns that the soul must be purified of its "original sin" (impurities) before a permanent union can be achieved.</summary>
<keywords>Conjunction, Fourth Gate, George Ripley, Philosopher's Stone, Alchemy, Separation, Apothecaries, Soul and Body</keywords>

--- Page 169 ---
<meta>This page continues the "Fourth Gate" of Conjunction, expanding on the different types of alchemical unions required to stabilize the elements after they have been separated and purified.</meta>

<page-num>145</page-num>
<header>Of Conjunction.</header>

<margin>4.</margin> Philosophers mention two kinds of conjunctions.
The first is "gross," occurring when the body is rejoined <note>original: "reincendat"; literally "re-kindled," referring to a crude or physical mixing of substances.</note> with mercury.
But let that pass, and pay attention to the second kind,
Which, as I said, is performed after separation.
In this process, the parts that were left are joined together <note>original: "collygate"; from the Latin *colligare*, to bind or tie together.</note>;
And thus they are advanced to a state of most perfect balance <note>original: "temperance"; in alchemy, the ideal proportional harmony of the four elements.</note>,
So that never again can there be any conflict <note>original: "repugnance"; the natural tendency of opposing elements, like fire and water, to reject one another.</note> between them.

<margin>5.</margin> Thus, separation allows a true conjunction to be achieved
Between water, air, earth, and fire.
In order that every element may be led into the others,
And remain that way forever according to your desire,
Do as laborers do with clay and mud <note>original: "myer"</note>:
Mix them into a thick consistency and do not make them too thin,
For in that way, you will more quickly succeed in drying them out.

<margin>6.</margin> But there are three ways to perform this conjunction.
The first is called "Diptative" <note>A term referring to a binary union, or a union of two parts.</note> by philosophers,
Which must occur between the "Agent" and the "Patient" <note>The active and passive principles in a chemical or philosophical reaction.</note>,
Which are Male and Female, Mercury and living sulphur <note>original: "sulphure vive"; native or unrefined sulphur, considered a primary alchemical principle.</note>;
It is the thriving union of matter and form, and of the thin with the thick.
This lesson will undoubtedly help you
To truly bring about our conjunction.

<margin>7.</margin> The second way is called "Tryptative" <note>A term referring to a tripartite union, or a union of three parts.</note>,
Which is a conjunction made of three things:
Of body, soul, and spirit, until they no longer struggle against each other.
This trinity must be brought to a perfect unity;
For just as the soul must be the bond to the spirit,
So the soul must knit itself to the body.
Do not let this lesson slip from your mind.

8. &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The third way, and also the last of all,
Which joins four elements together to remain,
Philosophers contentedly call it *Tetraptative* <note>original: "Tetraptative"; likely derived from the Greek for "four," referring to a union of all four elements.</note>,
And especially *Guydo de Montayno*, whose fame goes wide;
And therefore it is the most praiseworthy method at this time.
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;In our *Conjunction*, four elements must be gathered together,
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;In due proportion first, which previously were separated.

9. &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Therefore, just as the woman has fifteen veins,
And the man but five for the act of her fertility <note>original: "fecundyte"</note>,
It is required in our *Conjunction* first, I mean,
So must the man, our *Sun*, have three parts of his water;
And (nine) his wife, which must be three to him <note>This refers to the specific alchemical ratios of mercury (water/wife) to the solid body (Sun/man) required for a successful reaction.</note>:
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Then like will have joy to dwell with like,
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;More of *Conjunction* I need not tell.

10. &nbsp;&nbsp;Therefore, I will conclude this chapter very soon,
Charging you to make only one gross *Conjunction* <note>original: "Groce"; meaning a crude or physical mixing of substances.</note>,
For rarely have harlots borne children,
And so you shall never obtain our *Stone*,
Unless you allow the woman to lie <note>original: "lygg"</note> alone;
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;So that after she has conceived by the man,
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Her womb <note>original: "Matryce"</note> is then shut off from all others.

11. &nbsp;&nbsp;For those who continually add crude material to crude material,
Opening their vessels and letting their matter cool <note>original: "kele"</note>:
They do not nourish the conceived sperm, but delude
Themselves, and ruin their work in every part;
If you therefore desire <note>original: "lyst"</note> to do well,
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Close up the womb and nourish the seed,
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;With continual and temperate heat if you wish to succeed <note>original: "spede"</note>.

<margin>12.</margin> And when your vessel has stood for five months,
And clouds and eclipses <note>original: "Clypsys"; referring to the *nigredo* or "blackness" stage of the process where the matter darkens.</note> are each passed;

<note>In alchemy, the "Child" or "Infant" represents the emerging Philosopher's Stone, which must be "fed" with additional mercury or "moist" material to grow in strength.</note>

->And the water has gained a retaining power from the earth;<-
->These four elements are made one, never more to struggle.<-

<margin>14.</margin> And all our intention depends on two things,
On the dry and the moist, which are two opposites;
On the dry, that it brings the moist to fixation <term>Fixation: the process by which a volatile or fluid substance is made stable and resistant to heat.</term>,
And on the moist, that it gives liquefaction <note>the ability to melt or flow like wax</note> to the earth,
So that from them, thus tempered together, may come forth
->A balanced state not as thick as the [solid] Body is,<-
->Nor as thin as water, certainly.<-

<margin>15.</margin> Loosening and knitting <note>original: "Losyng and knyttyng"; the English equivalent of the famous alchemical maxim *solve et coagula*, or "dissolve and congeal."</note> are therefore the two principles
Of this difficult *science*, and its most essential poles;
Even though there are many more other principles,
Like shining banners <note>original: "fanells"; likely meaning signals or vanes that show the way.</note> which I shall show:
Proceed therefore to another wall
->Of this strong castle of our wisdom,<-
->So that you may enter within at the Fifth Gate.<-
